scope: Bounded source-clause audit of 8.1–8.18P, visually checked on official Physics specification PDF pages 33–34 / printed 27–28. All local requirements remain partial; principal-region diagrams are authored schematics, not observational datasets.
identifierPolicy: Requirement suffixes r1, r2, etc. are local editorial audit identifiers; only the parent reference is publisher-numbered.

parents.scopeNote: All seven named units remain explicit.

requirements.summary: Use kilograms for mass.
remainingChecks: Assess mass and weight distinction independently.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use metres for distance.
remainingChecks: Assess radius/altitude and km/m conversions.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use metres per second for speed.
remainingChecks: Assess speed conversions and significant figures.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use metres per second squared for acceleration.
remainingChecks: Assess equivalent numerical g and acceleration units.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use newtons for force.
remainingChecks: Assess gravitational force with supplied g.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use seconds for time.
remainingChecks: Assess minute/hour/second conversions.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Use newtons per kilogram for gravitational field strength.
remainingChecks: Assess field strength versus force.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: The three source bullets are separately retained; size statements describe the syllabus-level hierarchy.

requirements.summary: Recognise the universe contains billions of galaxies.
remainingChecks: Assess universe/galaxy/system hierarchy.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Recognise large galaxies contain billions of stars.
remainingChecks: Assess star versus galaxy distinctions without universalising galaxy size.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Locate the Solar System within the Milky Way.
remainingChecks: Assess nested locations and incorrect centre claims.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Cause of variation and examples of different worlds are separate.

requirements.summary: Explain variation in gravitational field strength.
remainingChecks: Assess mass and centre-distance dependencies separately.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Recognise different field strengths on planets, the Moon and Earth.
remainingChecks: Assess new-world g without assuming mass changes with location.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: All four named orbital cases are retained.

requirements.summary: Explain gravity keeping moons around planets.
remainingChecks: Assess inward force and tangential velocity on a labelled moon orbit.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain gravity keeping planets around the Sun.
remainingChecks: Assess curved paths and changing velocity.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain gravity keeping artificial satellites around Earth.
remainingChecks: Assess constant speed versus zero resultant force.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Explain gravity keeping comets around the Sun.
remainingChecks: Assess noncircular gravitational motion.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Comparison is qualified rather than claiming every orbit is identical.

requirements.summary: Compare comet, moon and planet orbits.
remainingChecks: Add calibrated orbit diagrams and comparisons of central body, eccentricity and plane.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Circle formula is not applied to local speeds on elongated ellipses.

requirements.summary: Use orbital speed = 2πr/T.
remainingChecks: Calibrate inverse quantities, unit conversion, radius/altitude and allowed rounding.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Colour grouping is distinct from apparent brightness.

requirements.summary: Classify stars by colour.
remainingChecks: Assess colour ordering using unfamiliar star descriptions.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Surface temperature is not substituted for core temperature.

requirements.summary: Relate stellar colour to surface temperature.
remainingChecks: Assess colour/size/brightness distinctions.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: All four specified stages are retained; additional detailed evolution remains out of the bounded audit.

requirements.summary: Describe formation from a nebula.
remainingChecks: Assess gravity, contraction and heating.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Describe the main-sequence stage of a Sun-like star.
remainingChecks: Assess hydrogen fusion and the stage sequence.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Describe the red-giant stage.
remainingChecks: Assess core fuel change and expanding outer layers.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Describe the white-dwarf remnant.
remainingChecks: Assess hot remnant versus ongoing main-sequence fusion.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: The high-mass route is qualified: slightly above solar mass is not an automatic supernova.

requirements.summary: Describe evolution of high-mass stars.
remainingChecks: Calibrate red-supergiant, supernova and alternative-remnant explanations.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2: standard distance and magnitude direction are both explained.

requirements.summary: Interpret absolute magnitude as brightness at a standard distance.
remainingChecks: Assess negative magnitudes, consistent bands and apparent/absolute distinctions.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2: these are local drawing criteria under the one publisher statement.

requirements.summary: Draw correctly directed H–R axes.
remainingChecks: Assess temperature and absolute-magnitude axis reversals.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Place the main sequence on an H–R diagram.
remainingChecks: Calibrate placement tolerance and distinguish population pattern from evolution.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Place giant and supergiant regions.
remainingChecks: Assess cool luminous stars and the bright upper region.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Place white dwarfs.
remainingChecks: Assess hot/faint interpretation and drawing criteria.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2: cosmic history and supporting arguments are separated.

requirements.summary: Describe evolution from an early hot dense universe.
remainingChecks: Assess expansion, cooling and later structure without inventing a central explosion.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Describe arguments supporting the Big Bang model.
remainingChecks: Calibrate evidence versus claims beyond the model.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2: the two named observations must remain distinct.

requirements.summary: Describe red-shift as Big Bang evidence.
remainingChecks: Assess observed trend followed by model inference.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Describe CMB radiation as Big Bang evidence.
remainingChecks: Assess cooled early thermal radiation rather than present-day starlight.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2: elementary approach/recession examples specify line-of-sight motion.

requirements.summary: Describe observed frequency changes with relative source motion.
remainingChecks: Assess approach and recession without changing source frequency.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

requirements.summary: Describe observed wavelength changes with relative source motion.
remainingChecks: Assess wavelength/frequency opposition and fixed vacuum light speed.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2: the specified equation is taught with its small-shift approximation limit.

requirements.summary: Use fractional wavelength change = recession speed / light speed.
remainingChecks: Calibrate inverse wavelength, difference/reference denominator, unit and precision cases.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2: statistical distance trend is not a claim about every nearby galaxy.

requirements.summary: Describe galactic red-shift at different distances.
remainingChecks: Assess trend/scatter graphs and local-motion exceptions.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

parents.scopeNote: Paper 2: a measured trend supports expansion without identifying Earth as its centre.

requirements.summary: Explain why galactic red-shifts support expansion.
remainingChecks: Calibrate observation/inference reasoning and non-central-observer explanations.
Independent assessment-family coverage is not yet validated.

supportingReferences.role: Factual cross-checks and further reading only. Pearson specification/mark schemes remain authoritative for requirements and assessment. No third-party graphics or prose copied.
